title: Rare Orange Baby Sea Turtle Looks Like Pumpkin Spice
summary:
In August, a Florida beachgoer spotted a baby loggerhead turtle racing toward the ocean. Its shell looked orange-brown, like fall colors. Michael Landress nicknamed it "Pumpkin Spice," even though he says he does not like pumpkin spice drinks.

Most loggerhead hatchlings have brown top shells and tan or yellow undersides. Biologist Daniel Evans of the Sea Turtle Conservancy says colors as bold as pumpkin spice are rare.

Color helps hatchlings hide in floating seaweed. Usual browns blend in. Odd colors stand out more to predators. That is one reason adults usually do not keep such bright hatchling colors.

Loggerheads are named for their big heads. Florida has one of the world's largest nesting groups, but the species is still listed as endangered or threatened. Accidental catch in fishing gear is a big danger. This unusual hatchling is a fun reminder that nature can surprise us.
